evidence:
Read instruction.md cold (sha256 58b592ff45aa5aaf0b9078c518c653a2367396c9f6cc058ce1ba825f9d3e5ecc, 19 lines, 9 prose paragraphs) plus both notes it points to (hireops_rules.md 23ba10bf..., integration.md 4eddd8a3...). It reads as a team lead asking for an app: opens 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (instruction.md:1), states the core difficulty in user terms ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled', :1), and frames edge cases as personal needs with reasons ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none', :3; 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor', :5). No numbered lists, no shall/must table, no feature matrix in instruction.md; grep found only 2 'must', 1 "mustn't", 2 'has to' across the brief. Layout/naming freedom is explicit ('layout and names are yours', :11; 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', :15). The only spec-like paragraph is the runtime contract (:15-19: node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH, seed path, accounts), which the template convention and row 4 require and which is phrased conversationally; it prescribes no framework beyond the template-fixed Node/Express/SQLite runtime (template integration.md lines 1-14 are carried verbatim) and no file layout or endpoint list. The Colderwater lesson-5 self-check line is present in requester voice (:13).
Lesson 12 check (notes as acceptance checklist), applied to every section of hireops_rules.md: the notes are written as the team's 'working rules' (hireops_rules.md:1-5, 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are up to you'), and most tightened edge cases carry a user reason: concurrency ('Several of us work the same board, so...', :78), optimistic UI ('When I move a card I want to see it move straight away', :86), bulk ('I often select two or more cards', :92), live updates ('We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands', :127), long threads ('Some conversations run long, so...', :151), candidate privacy ('Candidates are outside the company, so...', :200), deployment ('Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder', :207; integration.md:16-23 'We copy /app as ordinary files...'). Bullets are limited to who-may-do-what role lists (:70-74, :137-141, :165-167); tables are a role legend (:15-20) and candidate wording data (:191-198), not acceptance matrices. Criteria (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml e.g. hro_undo, hro_two_people, hro_moves) are multi-step scenarios, not one-to-one restatements of note sentences.
Residual spec-flavoured spots, judged Note-level not Fail: HTTP status codes 401/403/404/409 (hireops_rules.md:22-24, :79) are stated as team policy with reasons ('so they can't even learn that it's there'; 'so whatever screen or tool sent the move can tell them'); 'every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves' (:78-79) hints at the mechanism but is justified by the multi-user reason and leaves transport free; the Undo section (:97-104) is the densest rule-list paragraph with no 'why' beyond the first-person framing. None is a numbered acceptance list or a build recipe of framework/file layout/endpoint list as the quality-checks.md row-1 defect definition names. Adversarial angle: a conforming alternative app with different routes, labels, ids or layout is not disadvantaged by the brief's wording, since it explicitly disclaims those; this row grades prose shape only, so no broken-app counterexample applies. Workbook row 1 (Quality Checks and Internal Quality Checks sheets, column E empty, no internal annotation) and skill reference quality-checks.md section 1 applied. No runtime evidence is required for this text-only row; raw-evidence-index.json was opened (input_sha256 matches) but bears on no row-1 claim.
suggested_fix: Optional polish only (not required for Pass): give the Undo section (hireops_rules.md:97-104) one requester-voice reason sentence, as lesson 12 recommends, to keep it from reading as a rule list.
